_**The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker**_[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-2) is a 2002 [action-adventure game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action-adventure_game "Action-adventure game") developed and published by [Nintendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo "Nintendo") for the [GameCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube "GameCube"). An installment in [_The Legend of Zelda_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda "The Legend of Zelda"), it was released in Japan on December 13, 2002, in North America on March 23, 2003, and in Europe on May 2, 2003.

The game is set on a group of islands in the Great Sea, a departure for the series. The player controls the series' main protagonist [Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Link_(The_Legend_of_Zelda) "Link (The Legend of Zelda)") as he attempts to save his younger sister from the evil sorcerer [Ganondorf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganondorf "Ganondorf") and becomes embroiled in a struggle for the [Triforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triforce "Triforce"), a sacred wish-granting relic. Aided by allies including pirate captain [Tetra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetra_(The_Legend_of_Zelda) "Tetra (The Legend of Zelda)") – an incarnation of [Princess Zelda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Zelda "Princess Zelda") – and a talking sailboat named the [King of Red Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Red_Lions "King of Red Lions"), Link sails the ocean, explores islands, and traverses dungeons to acquire the power necessary to defeat Ganondorf. Wind, which facilitates sailing, plays a prominent role and can be controlled with a magic conductor's baton called the Wind Waker.

_The Wind Waker_ was directed by [Eiji Aonuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiji_Aonuma "Eiji Aonuma") and produced by [Shigeru Miyamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeru_Miyamoto "Shigeru Miyamoto") and [Takashi Tezuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takashi_Tezuka "Takashi Tezuka"). Development began in 2000. It retains the basic 3D gameplay of its predecessors, _[Ocarina of Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocarina\_of\_Time "Ocarina of Time")_ and _[Majora's Mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majora's\_Mask "Majora's Mask")_, but the team chose to avoid the realistic graphics of previous games. Instead, they implemented a distinctive cartoon-like art style created through [cel shading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cel_shading "Cel shading").

At its release, _The Wind Waker_ received critical acclaim for its visuals, gameplay, level design, music, and story. The art direction proved divisive among players and contributed to comparatively weak sales; the game sold 4.6 million copies, far below the 7.6 million sold by _Ocarina of Time_. As a result, Nintendo changed directions with the next major _Zelda_ installment, the more realistically styled _[Twilight Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Twilight\_Princess "The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess")_. _The Wind Waker'_ s reputation improved over time; with retrospective analyses, it is now considered [one of the greatest video games ever made](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_video_games_considered_the_best "List of video games considered the best"). _The Wind Waker_ popularized the "[Toon Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toon_Link "Toon Link")" character, and received two direct sequels for the [Nintendo DS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_DS "Nintendo DS"), _[Phantom Hourglass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phantom\_Hourglass "Phantom Hourglass")_ (2007) and _[Spirit Tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Spirit\_Tracks "The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks")_ (2009). A [high-definition remaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remaster "Remaster"), _The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD_, was released for the [Wii U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U "Wii U") in September 2013. The original version of the game was re-released as a launch title for [Nintendo Switch 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch_2 "Nintendo Switch 2") as part of the [Nintendo Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Classics "Nintendo Classics") service on June 5, 2025.

## Gameplay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Gameplay")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/08/The_Legend_of_Zelda_The_Wind_Waker_screenshot.jpg/250px-The_Legend_of_Zelda_The_Wind_Waker_screenshot.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Legend_of_Zelda_The_Wind_Waker_screenshot.jpg)

_The Wind Waker_'s cel-shaded art style makes use of real-time lighting and effects like [depth-of-field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_of_field "Depth of field") blur, making the game look stylistically similar to a cartoon and setting it apart from other games in the series.

_The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker_ is an [action-adventure game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action-adventure_game "Action-adventure game") with [role-playing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Role-playing_video_game "Role-playing video game") elements. The control scheme is comparable to its predecessors: the player moves the protagonist Link in three dimensions from a [third-person perspective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-person_perspective "Third-person perspective").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):8, 16 Link fights with a sword and shield as well as a variety of other weapons and items. He interacts with [non-player characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-player_character "Non-player character") and objects via the action button.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):9, 12, 16-18 Like the previous games, _The Wind Waker_ features a targeting system allowing Link to "lock on" and constantly face an enemy or target.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):12, 19 A new feature is the ability to move the [camera system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_camera_system "Virtual camera system") around Link.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):8, 11 Onscreen meters track Link's [health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_(gaming) "Health (gaming)") and magic; Link can expand his health meter by finding "heart containers" and container pieces in the game.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):11, 28

The game world comprises 49 gridded sections of the "[Great Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Sea_(The_Legend_of_Zelda) "Great Sea (The Legend of Zelda)")", each containing an island or island chain. Some must be explored to continue the story, while others are optional.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-4) Like all _Zelda_ games, _The Wind Waker_ features several dungeons—large, enclosed areas where Link fights enemies, finds items, and solves puzzles to continue. Each dungeon quest concludes with a battle against a [boss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boss_(video_games) "Boss (video games)"), a singularly powerful enemy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-5) In addition to the main story, the game includes many [sidequests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidequest "Sidequest"), minor objectives the player can optionally complete to attain rewards. For example, Link can use the "Picto Box" – an in-game camera – to take pictures to fulfill quests.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-6)

Throughout the game, Link acquires items and weapons that provide new abilities.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):20-21 Items are often needed to reach certain areas, defeat bosses or other enemies, and advance the story. For example, the [grappling hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grappling_hook "Grappling hook") is necessary to pass obstacles and defeat the boss in the Dragon Roost Cavern dungeon; it can then be used to enter previously inaccessible areas elsewhere. The "Tingle Tuner" is a special item allowing a second player to control the character [Tingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tingle_(character) "Tingle (character)") if the system is connected to a [Game Boy Advance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Advance "Game Boy Advance") by a [link cable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube_%E2%80%93_Game_Boy_Advance_link_cable "GameCube – Game Boy Advance link cable").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):20, 25

### Wind and sailing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Wind and sailing")]

A significant portion of the game is spent sailing between islands on Link's boat, the [King of Red Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Red_Lions "King of Red Lions"). The boat's sail is driven by wind that blows across the game world in one of eight directions; a [tailwind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tailwind "Tailwind") behind the boat will give it top speed, while sailing against the wind is difficult. The Great Sea features enemies and obstacles different from those found on land; additionally, some items serve new purposes while Link is aboard the King of Red Lions. The grappling hook, for example, serves as a crane for recovering sunken treasure.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):22-23 Link explores the sea with the help of a [sea chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_chart "Sea chart"), which can be updated with information on each square and island. Through the game, Link acquires additional charts pointing the way to treasure chests and significant locations. On land, dungeons feature similar maps.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-manual-3):14-15

Early in the game, Link receives the Wind Waker, a [baton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baton_(conducting) "Baton (conducting)") which allows him to control the wind and harness other powers by "conducting" specific melodies. The player controls the Wind Waker by moving the joypads to change pitch and [time signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature"). The first melody, the "Wind's Requiem", enables Link to change the wind's direction, allowing him to sail anywhere. Link can learn five other tunes for the Wind Waker, which provide abilities such as [warping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warp_(gaming) "Warp (gaming)") to other regions and turning night to day.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-7)

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

### Background and setting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Background and setting")]

Further information: [Fictional chronology of _The Legend of Zelda_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda#Fictional_chronology "The Legend of Zelda")

According to _[The Legend of Zelda: Hyrule Historia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Hyrule\_Historia "The Legend of Zelda: Hyrule Historia")_, Nintendo's official [_Legend of Zelda_ chronology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda#Fictional_chronology "The Legend of Zelda"), _The Wind Waker_ takes place in the Adult Era of the "Victorious Hero" timeline, one of several parallel timelines in which _Zelda_ games are set following the events of _[Ocarina of Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocarina\_of\_Time "Ocarina of Time")_. After Link, the Hero of Time, defeats Ganondorf and time-travels back to his childhood. A crisis emerges when Ganondorf returns, but Link does not. Centuries later, the people live on islands in the Great Sea. They preserve Link's story as a legend, but his kingdom's fate is unknown. The main character, a young boy also named Link, lives on Outset Island, where boys dress in green like the Hero of Time when they come of age.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-8)

### Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Plot")]

While Link is celebrating his coming of age, a gigantic bird drops the pirate captain [Tetra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetra_(The_Legend_of_Zelda) "Tetra (The Legend of Zelda)") into Outset Island's forest. Link rescues Tetra from monsters, but the bird carries off Link's younger sister Aryll. Tetra agrees to help Link find his sister, and they sail to the Forsaken Fortress, where the bird, the Helmaroc King, has been taking [girls with long ears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hylians "Hylians"). Link finds Aryll and other kidnapped girls, but the Helmaroc King captures him and takes him to a man in black, who orders Link throw into the sea.

Link is rescued at Windfall Island by a sentient sailboat, the King of Red Lions, who explains that the bird's master is a returned Ganondorf. To defeat him, Link must find the Hero of Time's power, which requires the three Pearls of the Goddesses. Link finds Din's Pearl on Dragon Roost Island, home of the avian [Rito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rito_(The_Legend_of_Zelda) "Rito (The Legend of Zelda)") and the dragon Valoo; Farore's Pearl in Forest Haven, home of the [Great Deku Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Deku_Tree "Great Deku Tree") and the plant-like [Koroks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koroks "Koroks"); and Nayru's Pearl with the water spirit Jabun on Outset Island. The King of Red Lions then takes Link to the Tower of the Gods, where he faces trials before descending beneath the ocean to a castle suspended in time. Here Link finds the Hero of Time's ultimate weapon, the [Master Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_Sword "Master Sword").

Link returns to the Forsaken Fortress. Tetra's crew arrive and rescue Aryll and the girls, but Ganondorf easily overpowers Link and Tetra and the Master Sword has lost its power. Ganon recognizes Tetra's Triforce necklace and realizes she is the incarnation of [Princess Zelda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Zelda "Princess Zelda") he is seeking. Link's Rito allies and Valoo save Link and Tetra from Ganondorf. The King of Red Lions brings the two back to the underwater realm, explaining it is the legendary kingdom of [Hyrule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyrule "Hyrule"), which the goddesses submerged long ago to contain Ganondorf while the people fled to the mountaintops. The King of Red Lions reveals himself to be Daphnes Nohansen Hyrule, the last King of Hyrule, and Tetra is his heir, the Princess Zelda, keeper of the Triforce of Wisdom.

Tetra remains in the castle while Link and Daphnes journey to the two sages who provided the Master Sword's power. They discover Ganondorf's forces murdered them both, so Link must awaken new sages, the Rito Medli and the Korok Makar, and guide them through the Earth and Wind Temples. The sages restore the Master Sword's power, but Daphnes learns that Ganondorf has abandoned the Forsaken Fortress and fears an attack. They then track down the eight shards of the missing Triforce of Courage, once kept by the Hero of Time, and the gods recognize Link as the Hero of Winds.

Link and Daphnes return to Hyrule to discover that Ganondorf has captured Zelda. Link follows them to Ganon's Tower, defeating Ganon's minions before Ganondorf overcomes him. Ganondorf joins Link's and Zelda's Triforce pieces with his own Triforce of Power, forming the completed Triforce, which will grant his wish to rule the entire world. Before he can act, Daphnes appears and wishes that the Goddesses wash Ganondorf and Hyrule away, and also grant Link and Zelda hope for their own future. Link and Zelda battle Ganondorf with the Master Sword and magical arrows as water pours around them; with the final blow, the Master Sword turns Ganondorf to stone. Link and Zelda rise to the surface as Daphnes are submerged and Zelda returns to Tetra's form. After reuniting with their friends, the heroes sail off to find a new land.

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Development")]

### Game design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Game design")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/GameCube-Console-Set.png/250px-GameCube-Console-Set.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GameCube-Console-Set.png)

_The Wind Waker_ was an early project developed for the GameCube.

Nintendo's _Zelda_ team initiated plans for a new game early in the development of the GameCube system, before _[Majora's Mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majora's\_Mask "Majora's Mask")_ was completed for the [Nintendo 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_64 "Nintendo 64") in 2000. [Eiji Aonuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiji_Aonuma "Eiji Aonuma"), director of _Majora's Mask_, returned to helm the project, while [Shigeru Miyamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shigeru_Miyamoto "Shigeru Miyamoto") and [Takashi Tezuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takashi_Tezuka "Takashi Tezuka"), the creators of the _Zelda_ series, served as producers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNRoundtable-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10) Early concepts generally followed _Ocarina of Time_'s designs, with graphics enhanced for the new system's capabilities.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-MacDonald-11) The team hastily created a brief clip of Link fighting Ganondorf for a demonstration at the 2000 [Space World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Space_World "Nintendo Space World") exposition, where Nintendo announced the GameCube. The clip resonated with fans and commentators who hoped it previewed the next _Zelda_ game.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Plunkett-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-demo2000-13)

The _Zelda_ team, however, had exhausted its ideas for this style and format.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10) Aonuma hated the demo, finding it derivative of past _Zelda_ games.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-MacDonald-11) The team explored other directions until designer Yoshiki Haruhana created a cartoonish drawing of a young Link that caught their eye. Design manager Satoru Takizawa drew up an enemy [Moblin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moblin_(The_Legend_of_Zelda) "Moblin (The Legend of Zelda)") in a similar style, and the team seized on the new gameplay and combat possibilities afforded by the stylized cartoon aesthetic. To achieve this look, they used [cel shading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cel_shading "Cel shading") on 3D models, giving the look of an interactive cartoon.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-MacDonald-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Green-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-15) The developers built the game with [Alias/Wavefront](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alias/Wavefront "Alias/Wavefront")'s Maya 3D tool and a custom [game engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_engine "Game engine").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-16) Aonuma initially kept the development quiet as he worried that Miyamoto would take issue with the cartoon style.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Inness-17)

[![Image 8: refer to caption](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Eiji_Aonuma_at_E3_2013_%28further_cropped_3%29.png/250px-Eiji_Aonuma_at_E3_2013_%28further_cropped_3%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eiji_Aonuma_at_E3_2013_(further_cropped_3).png)

[![Image 9: refer to caption](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Shigeru_Miyamoto_20150610_%28cropped_2%29.jpg/250px-Shigeru_Miyamoto_20150610_%28cropped_2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shigeru_Miyamoto_20150610_(cropped_2).jpg)

[![Image 10: refer to caption](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/K%C5%8Dji_Kond%C5%8D_2015_%28cropped%29.jpg/120px-K%C5%8Dji_Kond%C5%8D_2015_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:K%C5%8Dji_Kond%C5%8D_2015_(cropped).jpg)

The director, co-producer and composer in 2013, 2015, and 2015, respectively: Eiji Aonuma, Shigeru Miyamoto, and Koji Kondo.

With this decision, development proceeded swiftly. The team quickly decided the setting would be islands in an ocean, determining it would provide interesting visuals and mechanics in the cel-shaded style. This in turn inspired the central sailing feature.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNRoundtable-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10) As Aonuma predicted, some features drew skepticism from producers Miyamoto and Tezuka.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Inness-17) For instance, they requested an explanation for the characters' exaggeratedly large eyes. Aonuma's team jokingly suggested having Link shoot beams from his eyes before deciding to have him focus his gaze on significant objects nearby, giving hints to observant players about what to do next.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-18) Miyamoto remained dubious of the art direction and reminded Aonuma that it was not too late to change course. Ultimately Miyamoto relented due to the team's enthusiasm about the cartoon style and the fact that it could have taken a decade to make a more realistic _Zelda_ with their resources.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Inness-17)

Nintendo presented a demo clip of the new game at the 2001 Space World.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-MacDonald-11) Response to the cel-shaded design was divided. While some attendees enjoyed the new look, there was backlash from disappointed fans who had hoped for a more realistic _Zelda_ like the previous year's demo.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-MacDonald-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Plunkett-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Fahs-19) Critics derisively dubbed the game "Celda".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Plunkett-12) Miyamoto was surprised at the response and decided to limit revealing further information about the game until the team finished a playable demonstration, hoping to shift focus from the graphics to the gameplay.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-George-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-21)

Miyamoto introduced a playable demo at the next year's [Electronic Entertainment Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_Entertainment_Expo "Electronic Entertainment Expo") (E3), alongside another upcoming _Zelda_ title for the GameCube, _[Four Swords Adventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Four\_Swords\_Adventures "The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures")_. Miyamoto encountered glitches while he attempted to demonstrate Link's new ability to use enemies' dropped weapons. However, reception was more positive than that for the Space World demo.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-George-20) The game received the 2002 [Game Critics Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Critics_Awards "Game Critics Awards") for Best Console Game at E3.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-22)_[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ editor Fran Mirabella said the cartoon look "works very nicely" and that "it feels very much like _Zelda_".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-23) The whimsical style was compared to _[A Link to the Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_A\_Link\_to\_the\_Past "The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past")_ and promotional artwork from previous _Zelda_ games. The E3 demo also introduced new features, such as the ability to connect to the Game Boy Advance and receive help from Tingle.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-24) However, the art direction continued to divide audiences.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Newman_2004_153%E2%80%93154-25)

Development continued through late 2002, with targeted release dates of December in Japan and early 2003 in North America.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Japanesetitle-26) During the final stages, two dungeons that fell behind schedule were cut and replaced with a quest to recover Triforce pieces around the Great Sea. Elements of these dungeons were recycled for later _Zelda_ games.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-MacDonald-11) On October 15, 2002, Nintendo revealed the game's Japanese subtitle, _Kaze no Takuto_ (_Wind Baton_), to emphasize the role of wind in the game.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Japanesetitle-26) The company announced the English title, _The Wind Waker_, on December 2 the same year.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-27) In the gap between the Japanese and North American releases, the designers reworked some segments, notably shortening the lengthy Triforce quest.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNreview-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-29)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Music")]

The music in _The Wind Waker_ was composed by Kenta Nagata, Hajime Wakai, [Toru Minegishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toru_Minegishi "Toru Minegishi"), and [Koji Kondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koji_Kondo "Koji Kondo").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-30) The sound team was significantly larger than for other contemporary projects to accommodate Nintendo's desire for a high caliber of work in the rushed development schedule.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNRoundtable-9) Koji Kondo, the primary composer for _The Legend of Zelda_ series, contributed to the score but did not serve as sound director.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-TeetselKondo-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-OteroKondo-32) However, the score incorporated some of his pieces from older _Zelda_ games, modifying them to emphasize the time passed between the stories.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNRoundtable-9)

The soundtrack is primarily environmental; it modulates between various tracks depending on location, time and other conditions.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-33) Much of the score is inspired by traditional Irish music and is overall lighter and more upbeat than previous scores in the series.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-35) The advancement of [MIDI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIDI "MIDI") technology allowed the soundtrack to more closely approximate the sounds of real instruments than was possible in previous installments. The score features strings, winds, brass, percussion, and wordless vocals. The vocals are especially prominent in the tunes Link conducts with the Wind Waker, singing in [D major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D_major "D major").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-36) Shigeru Miyamoto reportedly played the [mandolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandolin "Mandolin") featured in the "Title Theme".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-NintendoWorldReport-37)[Scitron Digital Content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scitron_Digital_Content "Scitron Digital Content") released a two-disc, 133-track [soundtrack album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack_album "Soundtrack album"), _The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker Original Sound Tracks_, on March 19, 2003.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-38)

## Release and promotion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: .mw-parser-output .vanchor>:target~.vanchor-text{background-color:#ebf4ff}@media screen{html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .vanchor>:target~.vanchor-text{background-color:#0f4dc9}}@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .vanchor>:target~.vanchor-text{background-color:#0f4dc9}}Release and promotion")]

_The Wind Waker_ was released on December 13, 2002, in Japan,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Japanesetitle-26) on March 24, 2003, in North America,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-39) and on May 2, 2003, in Europe.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-40) To promote the release, Nintendo offered a bonus disc as a [pre-order incentive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-order_incentive "Pre-order incentive") which included a GameCube port of _Ocarina of Time_ as well as its previously unreleased expansion, _[Ura Zelda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ura\_Zelda "Ura Zelda")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Schneider-41)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-42)_Ura Zelda_, largely an adaptation of _Ocarina of Time_ with some changes, including new dungeon challenges, had been developed for the Nintendo 64's [64DD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64DD "64DD")[peripheral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral "Peripheral"), but was shelved when that system failed. _Ura Zelda_ was named _Ocarina of Time Master Quest_ in North America and Europe.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Schneider-41)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-43)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Europedisc-44)_Ocarina of Time/Master Quest_ discs became popular items in their own right in North America, with some customers making and then cancelling pre-orders to get them. To avoid this issue in Europe, Nintendo released the item only in two-disc packages with _The Wind Waker_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Europedisc-44)

In May 2003, Nintendo bundled _The Wind Waker_ with limited edition GameCubes in North America and Europe.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-45) On November 17 that year, Nintendo launched another promotion via a [compilation disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundled_software "Bundled software"), _The Legend of Zelda Collector's Edition_. The disc includes playable versions of the [original _Legend of Zelda_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda_(video_game) "The Legend of Zelda (video game)"), _[Zelda II: The Adventure of Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zelda\_II:\_The\_Adventure\_of\_Link "Zelda II: The Adventure of Link")_, _Ocarina of Time_, and _Majora's Mask_, as well as a _Wind Waker_ demo and two featurettes. Never sold commercially, the _Collector's Edition_ was included in another GameCube bundle and was made available to existing GameCube owners who either registered their system or subscribed to _[Nintendo Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo\_Power "Nintendo Power")_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-46) The compilation became a coveted item among fans; in the United Kingdom and Ireland, the 1000 allotted copies were claimed within minutes. To satisfy frustrated customers there, Nintendo offered additional copies to those who purchased select GameCube games.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameSpot_UK-47)

### _The Wind Waker HD_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: The Wind Waker HD")]

[![Image 11: A comparison of the graphics of Wind Waker HD and the original GameCube release, Wind Waker, with the original on the top and the remake on the bottom.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/ea/Wind_Waker_HD_comparison_%28small%29.jpg/250px-Wind_Waker_HD_comparison_%28small%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wind_Waker_HD_comparison_(small).jpg)

Comparison of the graphics from _Wind Waker HD_ (bottom) with those from the original [GameCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube "GameCube") version

In 2013, Nintendo developed a [high definition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-definition_video "High-definition video") re-release of _The Wind Waker_, _The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD_, for the [Wii U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U "Wii U"). The inspiration came when staff converted elements from various games to explore the system's capabilities while planning for _[Breath of the Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Breath\_of\_the\_Wild "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild")_.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-48) The developers experimented with several _Zelda_ games, but were especially struck by how well _The Wind Waker_ translated into high definition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Kohler-49)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-50) When the team determined it would take less than a year to remaster the entire game, Aonuma approached Miyamoto about developing it. He faced considerable reluctance from management due to players' mixed response in 2003, but Miyamoto ultimately greenlit development as Nintendo staff had found that opinions of the game had warmed over the years.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Kohler-49) Aonuma served as producer, while Daiki Iwamoto served as director.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10) The soundtrack was updated by Kenta Nagata, Hajime Wakai, Asuka Hayazaki, and Atsuko Asahi. While the game was developed in-house at [Nintendo Entertainment Analysis & Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Entertainment_Analysis_&_Development "Nintendo Entertainment Analysis & Development") (EAD), high-resolution textures were produced with the help of a few external companies.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata_Asks:_The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Wind_Waker_HD-51) The entire project took six months to develop.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-52)

_The Wind Waker HD_ features high definition graphics and improved lighting.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Iwata-10) The [Wii U GamePad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U_GamePad "Wii U GamePad")'s touchscreen serves as a map and inventory, eliminating the need to toggle between gameplay and the menu interface. Players can use motion controls to control the Wind Waker.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-metro1-53) Some weapons, like the bow, can be aimed using the GamePad's gyroscope, as in _[Ocarina of Time 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Ocarina\_of\_Time\_3D "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D")_. The game supports [Off-TV Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-TV_Play "Off-TV Play"), which enables the player to play the game solely on the Wii U GamePad. The game can also be played on the [Wii U Pro Controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii_U_Pro_Controller "Wii U Pro Controller"), a controller similar to the one used in the original game.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Nintendo_Japan_overview-54) The developers made some changes to the gameplay as well: they introduced a new item, the "Swift Sail", allowing for faster sailing on the Great Sea.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_explains-55) They also streamlined the Triforce quest, improved the Picto Box, and replaced the Tingle Tuner, which had required connectivity with a Game Boy Advance, with a Tingle Bottle item that connected to the [Miiverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miiverse "Miiverse") service prior to its shutdown on November 8, 2017.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGN_definitive-56)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-57)

A limited-edition [console bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_bundling "Product bundling") that combines both a digital version of the game and the Deluxe Wii U console was released on September 20, 2013, in North America. The black console features a GamePad with a golden Hylian Crest and golden _The Wind Waker_-styled Hylian letters and symbols. A redemption code for a digital copy of _[The Legend of Zelda: Hyrule Historia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Hyrule\_Historia "The Legend of Zelda: Hyrule Historia")_ was also included.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Joystiq_release_date_NA-58) A Ganondorf figurine was released with a special edition copy of the game, available exclusively through [GameStop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameStop "GameStop").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Joystiq_release_date_NA-58)

### Switch 2 re-release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Switch 2 re-release")]

Coinciding with the launch of the [Nintendo Switch 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch_2 "Nintendo Switch 2") on June 5, 2025, Nintendo added the original GameCube version of _The Wind Waker_ to [Nintendo Switch Online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch_Online "Nintendo Switch Online")'s [Nintendo Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Classics "Nintendo Classics") library of emulated games. It was one of the first three GameCube titles released for Nintendo Classics, and is exclusive to the Switch 2 via the premium "Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack" subscription tier.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-59)

_The Wind Waker_ received widespread critical acclaim.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Newman_2007_p_100-82)[Review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") calculated a score of 96/100 based on 80 reviews, indicating "universal acclaim".[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Metacritic-61) It was the fourth game to receive a perfect score from the Japanese magazine _[Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu")_,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Famitsu-67)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-FamitsuNWR-68) and additionally earned perfect scores from _[Computer and Video Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer\_and\_Video\_Games "Computer and Video Games")_,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-CVGreview-63)_[Game Informer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game\_Informer "Game Informer")_,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameInformerreview-69)_[Game Pro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game\_Pro "Game Pro")_,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameProreview-70)_[Nintendo Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo\_Power "Nintendo Power")_,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-NP2003-75) and _Planet GameCube_.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-NWRreview-76) It received high marks from many other reviewers as well, although it did not reach the levels of critical acclaim that had greeted _Ocarina of Time_.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Newman_2007_p_100-82)

While often noting fans' ambivalence about the cel shading, critics praised the game's visuals. Reviewers likened the game to a playable cartoon,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNreview-28)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-CVGreview-63)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-EGMReview-65)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Eurogamerreview-66)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-NP2003-75) with several positively comparing the animation to the films of [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") and [Hayao Miyazaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki "Hayao Miyazaki").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameInformerreview-69)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameProreview-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-NGCreview-74) In particular, critics appreciated the characters' unique expressiveness,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-EGMReview-65)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Eurogamerreview-66)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Famitsu-67)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-FamitsuNWR-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameSpot-72) and found that the fine details and environments added richness to the game world.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNreview-28)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-EGMReview-65)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Eurogamerreview-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameInformerreview-69)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameSpot-72)_Famitsu_'s reviewers wrote that the rich design brings all the game's elements together into a cohesive whole.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Famitsu-67)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-FamitsuNWR-68)_[Electronic Gaming Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic\_Gaming\_Monthly "Electronic Gaming Monthly")_'s reviewers found the animation quality unparalleled in games and wrote that "_The Wind Waker_'s new look is as effective as it is unique".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-EGMReview-65) Matt Casamassina of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ said that though some fans hold distaste for the graphics, Nintendo's execution represented the pinnacle of the GameCube's capabilities and of cel shading technology.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNreview-28)[Jeff Gerstmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Gerstmann "Jeff Gerstmann") of _[GameSpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameSpot "GameSpot")_ said that skepticism about the visuals was "unfounded" and wrote that the character design "adds emotional weight" to the storyline.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameSpot-72) Steve Thomason of _Nintendo Power_ wrote that though he was initially skeptical, the visuals worked "brilliantly, framing the most enjoyable game play experience I've had since _Ocarina of Time_".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-NP2003-75)

Critics also lauded the gameplay, in particular the responsive control system, fluid combat, and puzzles.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGNreview-28)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-EGMReview-65)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Eurogamerreview-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-GameInformerreview-69) Several reviews noted the similarity of its gameplay to that of _Ocarina of Time_, though they praised enhancements such as the ability to move the camera, perform counterattacks, and use enemy ### Audience response and sales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Audience response and sales")]

Player response to the game remained divided over the cel-shaded design.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-89) Reception was comparatively warm in Japan, where various media commonly borrow an [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") aesthetic, but was much more divided in North America.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-90) Some players appreciated the design and Aonuma's vision, but others found it childish and too far removed from the more realistic designs of previous games.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Newman_2004_153%E2%80%93154-25) According to [Stephen Totilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Totilo "Stephen Totilo") of _[Kotaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotaku "Kotaku")_, much of the backlash came from a contemporary anxiety that Nintendo was losing its edge by focusing on games for children, as opposed to the more mature, realistic fare developed by competitors.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Totilo-91)

_The Wind Waker_ generated the most successful pre-order campaign in Nintendo history at the time.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-92) However, sales did not live up to expectations; director Aonuma noted that purchases were disappointing in both Japan and North America. Japanese sales suffered from a general decline in the video game market caused by consumers shifting away from games, a phenomenon known as "gamer drift".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_2007_1-93) The overall market remained strong in North America, but _The Wind Waker_'s sales were slow there and had declined markedly by the time they reached one million.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_2007_3-94)_The Wind Waker_ sold 4.6 million copies, far below the 7.6 million record set by _Ocarina of Time_.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-95) Nintendo of America attributed the game's comparatively weak North American sales in large part to the cel-shaded graphics, which turned off many players, particularly older teenagers who made up _The Legend of Zelda_'s traditional audience. Miyamoto further blamed a failure to introduce major innovations to excite established players or attract new ones.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_2007_1-93)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_2007_3-94)

### _The Wind Waker HD_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: The Wind Waker HD")]

_The Wind Waker HD_ was critically acclaimed; Metacritic calculated a score of 90/100 based on 70 reviews.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-metacriticHD-96) The improved graphics of the game from the original received positive commentary. [Dan Ryckert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Ryckert "Dan Ryckert") of _[Game Informer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game\_Informer "Game Informer")_ noted that the upgrade was immediately apparent, and that "the vivid colors and crashing waves of the flooded Hyrule [look] fantastic".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-game_informer_review_HD-97)_IGN'_ s Jose Otero stated that the game "looks great".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-IGN_review_HD-98) Andrew Fitch of _[Electronic Gaming Monthly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic\_Gaming\_Monthly "Electronic Gaming Monthly")_ claimed that the game "enhances the already excellent _Wind Waker_ visuals with HD flair".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-EGM_review_HD-99)

The game's first week sales in Japan were 30,000 physical copies.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-100) In the week following the release of _Wind Waker HD_, sales of the Wii U console increased by 685% in the UK.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-101) As of September 2023, it has worldwide sales of 2.37 million units.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-102)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Legacy")]

### Sequels and other media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Sequels and other media")]

Nintendo initially planned a direct sequel for the GameCube, developed by Aonuma's _Zelda_ team under the working title _Wind Waker 2_. However, _The Wind Waker_'s underwhelming reception in North America, combined with the downturn in the Japanese video game market, convinced Aonuma that the only avenue to success would be a more realistic _Zelda_ game that would appeal to the stronger North American market. He persuaded Miyamoto, who authorized development of a realistically styled game using _The Wind Waker_'s engine, _[Twilight Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Twilight\_Princess "The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess")_, which proved to be a major success for the GameCube and the newly released [Wii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wii "Wii").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_2007_1-93)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Aonuma_2007_3-94)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-103)

_The Wind Waker_ originated the variant of the Link character named "[Toon Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toon_Link "Toon Link")", who appeared in several later Nintendo games.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Fahs-19)_The Wind Waker_ received two direct sequels for the Nintendo DS handheld system. Wanting to continue _The Wind Waker_'s story and art style, in 2007 Aonuma produced _[Phantom Hourglass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Phantom\_Hourglass "The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass")_, which follows Link and Tetra as they explore new reaches of the Great Sea.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-104)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-105)_[Spirit Tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Spirit\_Tracks "The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks")_ (2009) is set roughly a century later and features a new Link and Zelda, the latter a descendent of Tetra, as they traverse New Hyrule with a magical train.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-106)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-107) Toon Link also returned in indirectly related _Legend of Zelda_ games such as _Four Swords Adventures_ (2004), _[The Minish Cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_The\_Minish\_Cap "The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap")_ (2005), and _[Tri Force Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Tri\_Force\_Heroes "The Legend of Zelda: Tri Force Heroes")_ (2015).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-Fahs-19)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-108) He also features as a playable character in Nintendo's _[Super Smash Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super\_Smash\_Bros. "Super Smash Bros.")_[crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossovers_in_video_games "Crossovers in video games")[fighting game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighting_game "Fighting game") series, and along with other _Wind Waker_ characters, in the 2016 _Zelda_ pastiche _[Hyrule Warriors Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyrule\_Warriors\_Legends "Hyrule Warriors Legends")_.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-109)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-110)

Conductors of the concert tour _[The Legend of Zelda: Symphony of the Goddesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Symphony\_of\_the\_Goddesses "The Legend of Zelda: Symphony of the Goddesses")_ have used custom-made Wind Waker batons.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-111)_The Wind Waker_ also influenced 2017's _[Breath of the Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Zelda:\_Breath\_of\_the\_Wild "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild")_, which features a similarly stylized art design, but with more realistic proportions.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-112)_Breath of the Wild_ also includes species from _The Wind Waker_ among other references, leading some fans to speculate that it follows the "Adult Timeline" established by _The Wind Waker_.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_The_Wind_Waker#cite_note-113)
